finding: INV-6 promises the free-text fallback is 'never the default and never silent'; in the state 'server chosen, reachable, serves ZERO tools' the fetch SUCCEEDS so entry.failure stays null, blockingFailure is null (no Alert), and usePicker is false purely because toolOptions.length === 0 — so the code silently renders the free-text Tool Input (line 269) with the generic description 'The exact name of the tool to call on that server.' and no stated reason. The author cannot tell an empty-catalog server from a working picker.

INV-6 names 'a tool may declare no schema' as one of the TWO cases that must carry a documented, visible reason; in the state 'tool chosen but describeToolSchema returns null' (absent schema, non-object schema, or zero declared properties — toolSchemaForm.ts:206-212) the code sets useGenerated=false and falls back to the generic key/value 'Arguments' editor with description 'Key/value pairs passed to the tool…' and NO explanation of why the generated form is absent. The unreachable-server case gets an Alert (line 239); the no-schema case gets nothing.

INV-3 makes the Tool field a picker and INV-6 forbids silent degradation; in the state 'saved workflow whose step.tool is NOT among the fetched tools' (renamed/removed upstream tool) the kit Combobox resolves selection as `byValue.get(current) ?? null` (sdk/packages/kit/src/kit/combobox.tsx:73), so the field renders EMPTY showing the placeholder while step.arguments/step.tool still hold the stale name. The stored value is neither shown nor flagged, and validation cannot catch it (WORKFLOW_TOOL_NO_TOOL only fires on an EMPTY tool), so the author sees a blank Tool field on a workflow that will still call the old tool.

INV-1 promises 'no raw schema/YAML key language ever reaches the person building a workflow'; the humanisation is applied ONLY inside BuilderValidationPanel. On the Save path the server runs validate_for_install (validate.rs:501-524) and returns AppError message '[semantic/WORKFLOW_PROMPT_MISSING] agent_1: step has neither prompt: nor prompt_file:', which the page surfaces verbatim via message.error(e.message) (and the store stores it raw at WorkflowBuilder.store.ts:338-343). Reachable whenever store.validation is null or stale — never-validated, a transient /validate-def failure (the store deliberately keeps the prior validation, line 106-109), the 400ms debounce race, or the prompt_file divergence the /validate handler documents (handlers/dev.rs:98-105 resolves prompt_file against a throwaway temp dir while install resolves against the real bundle root). humaniseFinding is never called on this path.

INV-6 requires the fallback's stated reason to be TRUE; entryForServerName resolves against McpServer.servers, whose initial state is `[]` (modules/mcp/stores/mcpServer/state.ts:6). While that list is still loading, an existing tool step's valid server resolves to the `unknown-server` failure and the author is shown 'This step points at a server called "X", which isn't one of the servers available to you' (line 163) plus the free-text fallback — a false, alarming reason in a transient state that then flips to the picker. The store already distinguishes a loading catalog (entry.loading); it does not distinguish a loading SERVER LIST.

INV-1's rule for HUMAN_COPY is 'say what the PERSON must do'; the new copy for WORKFLOW_SANDBOX_FLAVOR_REQUIRED ('the workflow needs a sandbox environment chosen for it') and WORKFLOW_UNKNOWN_FLAVOR ('pick one of the installed environments') direct an action the builder cannot perform: BuilderDef has no `sandbox` field and toWorkflowDef never emits one (WorkflowBuilder.store.ts:25-30, 51-63), while AddStepMenu still offers the 'Run code' step (stepForms.ts:59). Every builder workflow containing a sandbox step therefore validates with a blocking error whose humanised instruction points at a control that does not exist, permanently blocking Save. Root cause is pre-existing; the branch's new copy asserts the missing affordance as if it were present.

INV-6 says the fallback is 'never the default'; in the ordinary INITIAL state (no server chosen) blockingFailure deliberately excludes the 'no-server' failure, so no Alert renders and toolOptions is empty — the author's FIRST view of the Tool field is the free-text Input, i.e. the escape hatch IS the default. The store already authored the correct copy for this state ('Pick a server first to see the tools it offers.', ToolCatalog.store.ts:161) but the component never renders it; a disabled picker carrying that sentence would satisfy the invariant.

INV-4 promises one typed field per declared property and INV-6 requires the fallback's reason to be stated correctly; in the state 'tool declares more than SCHEMA_BUDGET.maxFields (24) properties', the overflow properties spill into the section labelled 'Additional arguments' whose description reads 'Extra values this tool did not declare. Usually empty.' — which is false for those keys, since the tool DID declare them. The overflow note in ToolArgumentsForm.tsx:248-251 says 'the rest can be set below', contradicting the section's own description.

Candidate: INV-5 (templating survives) not upheld in typed controls. REJECTED — verified upheld in every generated kind: isTemplateValue (toolSchemaForm.ts:263) is type-agnostic, a templated value renders as a text Input for switch/number/select/multiselect/json alike (lines 111-120), coerceToDeclared passes a template through untouched (toolSchemaForm.ts:300), a compact RefInsertMenu is attached to every field's label row, and the switch back to a typed control is one click (lines 83-94).

Candidate: a saved workflow with schema-undeclared arguments loses them on edit. REJECTED — splitArguments preserves them in `extra`, the free rows are seeded from `extra` when a schema exists (ToolStepForm.tsx:178-180), and both commit paths merge known+rows so neither half clobbers the other (lines 203-216). State verified upheld.

`markUnknown` and the `unknownNames` state it writes (line 47) have NO production caller and no test caller — a repo-wide grep finds only the definition. The 'unknown server name' case is instead handled purely by entryForServerName's derived failure, so this action and its state are dead.

`invalidate` is documented as 'used by "try again"' but has no caller: the unreachable-server Alert (ToolStepForm.tsx:239-246) is a bare warning with no retry action, and the entry is cached only for the component's lifetime. The design's INV-6 escape hatch therefore has no recovery path — an author whose server was momentarily down must unmount and remount the step form to get the picker back.

The store documents itself as a 'PRIVATE, per-builder catalog' whose id-keying means 'two names for one server share a fetch' and whose `inflight` guard exists because 'several fields read the same server in one render pass'. But defineLocalStore().use() allocates a store per COMPONENT INSTANCE (sdk/packages/framework/src/store-kit.ts:629-645) and StepConfigPanel remounts the step form on every selection via `key={step.id}` (StepConfigPanel.tsx:88) — so the catalog is per-tool-step-mount, not per-builder: listTools refires every time the author clicks between steps, and no cache or in-flight coalescing ever spans two steps.

The design calls the humanisation drift guard 'the guard that makes this real'. The emit-site scanner only records a code when the FIRST string literal in the call is one of "schema"|"semantic"|"security"; a future ValidationError emitted on any other layer contributes nothing and fails no assertion, so it would ship with the raw wire message reaching the author. The test asserts the scanner found >0 codes overall, which does not detect a single silently-skipped emit site.

`loading={entry.loading}` on the Combobox is unreachable: usePicker (line 160) already requires `!entry.loading`, so the picker only renders when loading is false. The loading state is handled entirely by the fallback Input's disabled/placeholder branch (lines 274-277), leaving the Combobox's loading skeleton dead.

`HUMANISED_CODES` is exported as 'the drift-guard surface' but has no production consumer; the actual guard is the Rust test's TEXTUAL scan of the file for `"CODE"` literals (validate.rs:2040-2046), which never reads this export. Its only consumer is validationCopy.test.ts.

The design names WorkflowElicitForm + workflowElicitSchema as the generated form's twin. Only the FieldSchema/TitledChoice TYPES were reused; the schema→control derivation was re-implemented: fieldKind (lines 152-195), choiceOptions (141) and enumOptions (145) duplicate the already-shipped isMultiSelectField / isTitledSelectField / selectOptions in WorkflowElicitForm.tsx (lines ~35-63), which handle the identical enum / anyOf / oneOf / items-enum cases. The design names CapabilitySelect (capabilities.tsx) as the tool picker's twin. The Tool picker was instead inlined in ToolStepForm — options built at lines 141-148 and the control at 258-268 — rather than added as a sibling export next to CapabilitySelect. The two entity pickers stacked on the same form are also different primitives with different label conventions: Server is a Select labelled `display_name || name`, Tool is a Combobox labelled `name — description`, so adjacent fields for the same class of value read and behave differently.
